candidates.evidence: Four measured peaks at 92.5, 162.4, 189.4 and 226.5 cm-1 (FWHM 3.2-8.2 cm-1). The strongest pair (162, 189) and the 92 and ~224 features match the Raman modes usually quoted for orthorhombic SnS (about 96 Ag, 163 B3g, 192 Ag, 218/224). Matching is from memory of the literature, not checked against a reference spectrum; positions differ by -3.5 to +2.5 cm-1, which is larger than the fit error.

Isostructural Pnma sibling with a similar A_g/B_3g mode set in the same window. Not verified against reference data here; Ge is lighter than Sn, so its modes would be expected at higher frequency, which weakens this candidate.
Same structure type, but its dominant modes are usually quoted near 108 and 150 cm-1, which do not match the strong 162 and 189 cm-1 lines here.

hint_reasoning: No material_hint was given (null), so there is nothing to test the spectrum against. The identification is from the four-peak pattern and its polarization behaviour only. The data window (60-382 cm-1) excludes the high-frequency modes and the Si line that would help discriminate between candidates.

peaks.assignment: SnS A_g mode (about 96 cm-1 in orthorhombic SnS literature); tentative
peaks.source: Raman mode values for orthorhombic SnS (Pnma), recalled from the literature (e.g. Vidal et al. 1981; Sinha et al. 2018), not verified in this environment. Pattern from per-angle fit: parallel is twofold-dominated (2theta harmonic 7.7k vs mean 7.9k, max at ~65 deg); crossed is 4theta-dominated (~11% of parallel mean, max at ~110 deg). Mixed, so classed 'other'.

peaks.assignment: SnS B_3g mode (about 163 cm-1 in literature); tentative
peaks.source: Raman mode values for orthorhombic SnS (Pnma), recalled from the literature (e.g. Vidal et al. 1981; Sinha et al. 2018), not verified here. Pattern measured: parallel = 11.0k(1+cos4(theta-18 deg)), crossed = 11.0k(1-cos4(theta-18 deg)); both reach ~0 at minima. Both A_g (traceless diagonal) and B_3g give this pattern in this geometry, so the irrep label is not fixed by polarization.

peaks.assignment: SnS A_g mode (about 192 cm-1 in literature)
peaks.source: Raman mode values for orthorhombic SnS (Pnma), recalled from the literature (e.g. Vidal et al. 1981; Sinha et al. 2018), not verified here. Measured: parallel constant at 17.8k (modulation <=3%), crossed 292 +- 113 (about 1.6% of parallel, consistent with zero). Constant parallel with zero crossed means equal in-plane diagonal components, which is compatible with an A_g mode.

peaks.assignment: SnS mode near 224 cm-1 (A_g or B_2g, unresolved); tentative
peaks.source: Raman mode values for orthorhombic SnS (Pnma), recalled from the literature (e.g. Vidal et al. 1981; Sinha et al. 2018), not verified here. Measured: parallel 12.1k with a 2theta harmonic of 3.1k (25% modulation, max at ~61 deg, min at ~151 deg), crossed 277 +- 120 (about 2% of parallel, consistent with zero). A two-component fit (218 + 226) is not favoured (BIC +12), so one peak is used.

properties.name: phase
properties.source: Four-peak frequency pattern and polarization of the measured modes compared with orthorhombic SnS literature; not confirmed against a reference spectrum.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: A single Raman spectrum of this kind does not carry a reliable layer-number signal without a reference or a shear/breathing mode; none is present in the 60-382 cm-1 window.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: No defect-activated (D-type) or disorder features are seen; the spectrum is too limited to assess defects quantitatively.

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: Absolute frequency offsets from the literature values (-3.5 to +2.5 cm-1) have no calibration standard to separate strain from calibration error.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: No carrier-sensitive mode shift or plasmon feature is resolved in this window.

artifacts.type: zero-valued dropout pixels (901 of 11628 points, spread across 60-382 cm-1; masked before fitting)

citations: Literature Raman mode table for orthorhombic SnS (Pnma), as reproduced in the SnS Raman literature (e.g. Vidal et al., 1981; Sinha et al., 2018). Values were recalled from memory and could not be checked in this environment; verify before relying on them.
limits: Angle-resolved data: 18 angles (0-170 deg, 10 deg steps) in parallel and crossed configurations, 1 cm-1 step, 60-382 cm-1. Per-point noise about 140 counts on a background near 240 counts, so per-angle amplitude errors are about 450 (162 cm-1), 450-500 (93, 189) and 750 (226). Peak amplitudes were obtained by fitting Lorentzians with positions and widths fixed to the config-averaged parallel fit, with a linear background.

Cosmic-ray spikes: none found. A robust single-point excursion scan (6 sigma threshold) returned no hits, and all intensity maxima sit on multi-point peaks. Only the zero-valued dropout pixels were removed.
Window ends at 382 cm-1, so Si (520.7 cm-1) and higher-frequency SnS modes and second-order bands are not measured. The absence of Si is expected for a suspended sample but cannot be checked here.

Absolute frequency calibration is not verified (no standard lamp or Si reference in this window). Position uncertainties from the fit are about 0.03 cm-1 (statistical); a systematic offset of about 1-2 cm-1 is plausible.
Literature matching is from memory and was not verified. The residuals against the literature values (-3.5, -0.6, -2.6, +2.5 cm-1) are not a consistent offset, so the identification is tentative.

Polarization origin: the zero of the angle axis is unknown. Phases (fourfold maxima at about 18 deg, twofold maximum at about 61-65 deg) are relative to the stage zero, not to crystal axes, so they cannot fix the irrep assignments.
Ag (traceless diagonal) and B_3g modes both give fourfold patterns with a 45-degree offset in this backscattering geometry, so irrep labels for the 162 and 93 cm-1 modes are tentative.

Pattern for 226 cm-1 (twofold in parallel, crossed about zero) is not what a single diagonal Raman tensor gives in this geometry, so it may be a superposition or may reflect limited crossed-channel sensitivity. The 218/224 doublet is not resolved; a two-component fit is not favoured, but it cannot be excluded at this signal-to-noise.

Crossed-channel leakage: the crossed intensities of 189 and 226 are about 1.6-2% of parallel, consistent with zero but not strictly zero. The crossed/parallel ratio also assumes equal throughput for both configurations, which was not calibrated.
No second-order or weak modes above 3 sigma residual were found in the config-averaged fit. Weak features near 107-150 cm-1 are at the noise level and were not claimed.

Layer number, thickness, stacking, and stoichiometry cannot be determined from these data. Temperature (295 K) is given in the metadata and was not verified by a Stokes/anti-Stokes or peak-width analysis.
